subject: QBR runway: capacity & unit-econ asks (prep packet + short read)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR runway: capacity & unit-econ asks (prep packet + short read)

Team —

As we stitch the QBR narrative on capacity and unit economics, I pulled together a short set of asks so leadership has clean artifacts to review. Please treat this as the single source for what's due by EOD Wednesday (June 2):

1) Capacity forecast (by SKU / instance type & region) — weekly view for next 13 weeks plus best/worst demand scenarios. Highlight any known infra ops constraints (maintenance, driver upgrades, region outages).

2) Unit-econ sensitivity table — show per-token cost across batching, KV-prefix cache hit rates (0/30/60%), and quantization profiles (fp16/int8). Single-tab summary + model assumptions.

3) Experiment readouts — three slides max: (a) batching latency vs cost tradeoff, (b) cache warm-up SKU impacts, (c) best candidate for immediate runway lift. Link the notebooks.

4) SLA & fallback ask list — any capacity reservations or SLA exceptions we should put on the QBR deck (e.g., priority pool with X% reserved).

I've attached an initial runway model (qbr_runway_modeling.xlsx) and a short operational primer on prefix/KV caching (prefix_cache_playbook.pdf). Internal links to modeling and experiment notebooks are below.

Plan: we will synthesize into 6 slides for execs + an appendix with sensitivity tabs. I will take the slide deck and finalize narrative on Thursday morning.

If you have blockers (data access, missing telemetry), call them out in replies so we can escalate to infra immediately.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0123

Attachments: qbr_runway_modeling.xlsx (Excel), prefix_cache_playbook.pdf (PDF)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR runway: capacity & unit-econ asks (prep packet + short read)

Thanks — good list. A couple quick clarifications and an extra ask from leadership:

- On the capacity forecast: please include both committed (Dedicated) capacity and elastic (hosted) consumption separately. Leadership wants to see the marginal cost of serving additional hosted requests beyond committed pools.
- For unit-econ, add a small column for engineering effort (low/med/high) to indicate how operationally costly a lever is to implement (e.g., aggressive batching may need code changes).
- New ask: include a brief blurb (1–2 bullets) on how the rollout of the new kernel selection heuristics would affect the 13-week runway (best / expected / conservative). Markus, can you add that to the sensitivity tab?

I'll slot this into the OKR check-in so we can ensure deck aligns to our metrics ask.

-Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
VP, Platform Strategy
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

On Sun, May 30, 2027 at 09:12 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
>
> As we stitch the QBR narrative on capacity and unit economics, I pulled together a short set of asks so leadership has clean artifacts to review. Please treat this as the single source for what's due by EOD Wednesday (June 2):

Thanks — this is actionable. Quick notes from infra/serving:

- I'll populate the kernel-selection delta into the sensitivity tab. Early numbers show 8–12% token-cost improvement for Llama-family 70B when the heuristic prefers fused attention kernels at seq_len <= 1024; will add conservative and optimistic lines.
- Batching: we have two experiment cohorts. Cohort A (aggressive micro-batching + async IO) reduces cost ~18% at a 15% p95 latency penalty for high-concurrency routes; Cohort B (adaptive batching by route) is ~10% cost with negligible p95 change. I'll include both in the experiments sheet with CPU/GPU util traces.
- Cache: realistic warm-up assumptions matter. I've modeled 0/25/50/75% prefix cache hit scenarios; the delta between 0 and 50% is ~22% unit cost reduction for chat workloads with long prefixes. Note: cache storage cost and eviction churn are included in next tab.

Attachments: I exported two small artifacts into the Drive folder (kernel_delta.csv, batch_experiment_traces.tar.gz).

I'll update the workbook and share a short 2-slide technical appendix by EOD.

-Markus

--
Markus Klein
Director, Serving Infrastructure
markus_klein@redwood.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: QBR runway: capacity & unit-econ asks (prep packet + short read)

Acknowledged — we have the telemetry hooks but a couple operational notes:

- Telemetry: cost-by-token and cache-hit metrics are live on staging but we need a short retention window (14 days) of per-request traces to run the sensitivity in full fidelity. Ops can turn this on for the test window; I'll approve.
- Procurement: looping in CloudMarket procurement for a quick check on reserved-pool pricing changes that may land in mid-June. If they confirm, we should include a sensitivity where committed pool pricing improves 5% (that materially moves the runway).
- Ask to Jordan: please flag whether any customer-facing SLA language will change if we enable aggressive batching on customer routes (we need legal/CS signoff).

I'll approve Ops to flip the staging retention and mark items as green once I have the procurement note.

Irene
